tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
A line that crosses two parallel lines is called a **transversal**. For example, the line $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{EF}$ in the diagram below is a transversal.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14178066/assets/cdae3e21ca7b66c756e047b2f71dd03d1320a947e7477f6b025dacef95321399.png)

A pair of parallel lines with a transversal form a set of $8$ angles, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14178066/assets/a4465bbe051f978925e704cc40ced894c4e8c6625c53c7bd944a93c123359ab9.png)

This set of eight angles can be grouped into two categories:

- We have four pairs of **vertical angles**:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14178066/assets/e010db0c586e29e8ae640842f1519da314455bb7520680b80530799509058df3.png)

- We also have four pairs of so-called **corresponding angles**:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14178066/assets/d1b3f1ede08e3c20c80b7a23477491237e73a9b6691d93e6deabc5e5a4e0c57b.png)

Corresponding pairs of angles are located in the same position as each other relative to the parallel lines and on the same side of the transversal. Pairs of corresponding angles are congruent.

tutorials.name: A Worked Example
tutorials.problem:
Consider the following pair of parallel lines $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{AB} \parallel \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{CD},$ and the transversal $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{EF}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14178066/assets/af403ef4827e840a49d5a3bde36561d22a508d262b3ad15b830812aefc306286.png)

 What is the value of $x?$

First, note that $\angle DIF$ and $\angle BJI$ are corresponding angles. Therefore, they are congruent and thus have the same measure. This means we can write down the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠DIF & =m∠BJI \\ 3x-{20}^{∘} & =x+{10}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

To solve this equation, we first subtract $x$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-{20}^{∘} & =x+{10}^{∘} \\ 3x-{20}^{∘}-x & =x+{10}^{∘}-x \\ 2x-{20}^{∘} & ={10}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we add $20^\circ$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-{20}^{∘} & ={10}^{∘} \\ 2x-{20}^{∘}+{20}^{∘} & ={10}^{∘}+{20}^{∘} \\ 2x & ={30}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides by $2{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ={30}^{∘} \\ \frac{2x}{2} & =\frac{{30}^{∘}}{2} \\ \frac{\cancel{2}x}{\cancel{2}} & ={15}^{∘} \\ x & ={15}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=15^\circ.$
tutorials.title: A Worked Example
tutorials.content:
Consider the following pair of parallel lines $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{AB} \parallel \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{CD},$ and the transversal $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{EF}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14178066/assets/af403ef4827e840a49d5a3bde36561d22a508d262b3ad15b830812aefc306286.png)

 What is the value of $x?$

First, note that $\angle DIF$ and $\angle BJI$ are corresponding angles. Therefore, they are congruent and thus have the same measure. This means we can write down the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠DIF & =m∠BJI \\ 3x-{20}^{∘} & =x+{10}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

To solve this equation, we first subtract $x$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-{20}^{∘} & =x+{10}^{∘} \\ 3x-{20}^{∘}-x & =x+{10}^{∘}-x \\ 2x-{20}^{∘} & ={10}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we add $20^\circ$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-{20}^{∘} & ={10}^{∘} \\ 2x-{20}^{∘}+{20}^{∘} & ={10}^{∘}+{20}^{∘} \\ 2x & ={30}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides by $2{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ={30}^{∘} \\ \frac{2x}{2} & =\frac{{30}^{∘}}{2} \\ \frac{\cancel{2}x}{\cancel{2}} & ={15}^{∘} \\ x & ={15}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=15^\circ.$
